answer: A publisher hires agents to illustrate a fable set in a hollow onyx tower. To resist shill bidding, it fixes payment per commissioned scene before offers arrive, gives no signup bonus and pays each scene once. Inventing rival bidders cannot raise this posted rate, and aliases submitting the same scene cannot multiply payment. To earn more, an attacker must deliver additional commissioned work and pay submission fees. Acceptance needs independent quality checks; this blocks price manipulation by fake rivals but does not by itself prevent queue flooding.
